successors.name: Dutch East Indies
successors.text: Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

ledger.x: c. 1400: Cinnotabiq becomes Wajoq. 'It was founded in the 15th century, and reached its peak in the 18th century'; Cinnotabiq was 'transformed into Wajoq in the early 15th century' under La Tenribali; header 'c. 1400-1957'.
1610: closed in the year it opens.
1905: Wajo ends as a sovereign state.

wars.name: Gowa's wars of Islamisation against the Bugis states
wars.outcome: Gowa forced 'Soppeng to embrace Islam in 1609, Wajoq in 1610, and Bone in 1611'.

wars.name: Makassar War (Wajo's part)
wars.outcome: Wajo 'still refused to abide by the Treaty of Bungaya' (page, no date); the Makassar War page does not mention Wajo.

certainty.note: The page gives no frontier; Wajo's lands round the lakes were a federation of districts.
